newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl names conditions for tax talks with SPD.
newsitem.headline: Kohl names conditions for tax talks with SPD.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Monday a basic reduction in all private and corporate tax rates was an "essential point" for tax negotiations with opposition Social Democrats (SPD) this week.

In an open letter to SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine, Kohl also said the coalition intended to lower workers' social security contributions as part of a reform of Germany's pension, health and unemployment benefit systems.

"I think further talks on Wednesday only make sense...if there is a basic readiness to reach an understanding on these two points, and I would be grateful to you for an appropriate clarification," Kohl wrote.
Kohl and Lafontaine met without result last week but agreed to continue talks on a massive tax overhaul in an effort to avoid a battle through the parliamentary institutions.
The coalition wants to reduce taxes to revive the economy, cut near-record unemployment, and help Germany qualify for European economic and monetary union.

But the SPD, which can block most tax measures through its majority in the upper house, disagrees with the proposed top tax rate and other points in the plan put forward by Finance Minister Theo Waigel.
